## Claims the audit disputes

| ID | Paper claim | Verdict | Evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| D1 | With reliable timestamps, staleness is essentially eliminated (at most 0.2%). | **Overstated** | out_nat_date_new: 21.0% overall, 29.2% at a 90-day delay. The 0.2% figure holds only for uniform templates. |
| D2 | A shuffled order falls between the extremes (34.8%), consistent with order being the operative cue. | **Not supported as stated** | The shuffled cell uses mixed wording, whose matched baseline is 65.0%, not 100%. A pure positional rule predicts ~50%, and 34.8% is below that. |
| D3 | The effects are roughly additive (9.6 + 14.4 + 29.8 = 53 points). | **Arithmetic error** | 100 - 53.8 = 46.2, but the mixed condition is 65.0%. |
| D4 | The stale rate equals one minus archive coverage. | **Identity, not a result** | Holds to machine precision in every four-policy run because archiving removes the only competing record. |
| D5 | Recency-first review removes no conflicts. | **Structural** | The 40 updated records are the newest entries and nearly fill the 41-record budget, so recency cannot reach a conflict. The zero is a cap built into the store, not a property of recency as a signal. |
| D6 | The decay signal is not doing any work of its own. | **Untested** | Half-life is assigned by importance band, so the two policies are not independent; and importance is random, so neither has a real signal to use. Against a random-selection baseline decay is in fact +12.1 points of conflict-hit rate. |
| D7 | Adding dates returns all four configurations to 0%. | **Conditional on wording** | True for template/uniform wording; false for mixed wording (21.0%). |
| D8 | GLM-4-Plus follows no stable rule. | **Mislabelled** | 39 of 40 chains give the same verdict at all four delays and all three seeds; the choice is chain-determined and delay-invariant, which is a rule. |
